newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Don't underestimate Fiji, ABs warned.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Don't underestimate Fiji, ABs warned.

text.p: WELLINGTON, June 3 - Fiji's rugby tour has been low key so far but All Blacks selector Ross Cooper and Wellington Hurricanes coach Frank Oliver are warning that they should not be underestimated, NZPA reports.
The Fijians showed sound defensive qualities in beating the Central Vikings 19-10 in Palmerston North on Monday.
They showed that with further improvement they may prove a handful for the All Blacks at Albany in the one-off test on June 14.
"They played well against the Vikings, they showed a lot of commitment, particularly in the second half and they defended well," said Cooper, who was in Palmerston North to analyse the tourists.
"I was surprised how they hung in so well, I take my hat off, they're getting fitter and the pattern in the forwards especially is emerging quite strongly.
"They will continue to get better and they are getting better."
Cooper said he was impressed with the way Fiji showed discipline and control to shut out the Vikings who had numerous Super 12 squad members in their side.
He said he had no doubt Fiji would provide a stirring challenge at Albany.
"I think they will be very strong, they've got a good lineout with Emori Katalau (former Poverty Bay lock) and Api Naevo (Counties) and they took some good ball against the Vikings," Cooper said.
"They also have the ability to punish you severely at the turnover situation if you give them a chance."
Oliver warned the All Blacks that the Fijians possessed dangerously quick counter attacking ability.
"If you make one or two mistakes at that level, bang! you'll get punished especially by these guys," Oliver, who is also Central Vikings coach, said.
"They've got a lot of pace, while their flat-line defence was very good they're showing on tour that they have the pace to slide out of tackles.
"We won't strike guys that quick or strong in second division this year."
He warned the All Blacks they had to ensure possession was controlled because Fiji were showing they can be lethal on limited possession.
"If you make a mistake they will slaughter you. There is no substitute for pace all they've all got it," Oliver said.
"The more exposure they get to football here, because they come from so many different unions, the better they will get.
"And Brad (Johnstone -- Fiji coach) knows what he's doing."
With two wins out of three matches the Fijians today headed to Wanganui for their next game.
They play the tenacious second division newcomers in what should be a spirited encounter on Friday night.
